summary: Fail. Most of the previous finding is fixed. The fixed list now includes every sibling module both controllers load: native_merge.py, claude_review.py, handoff.py, qualification.py, readiness.py, readiness_index.py, action.py, native_review_index.py and json_data.py. These are read at both pinned revisions, and the evaluator revision also gets the policy_adoption scripts and supply JSON. Each file is read as data and bound to its repository, revision and verified Git blob. The candidate revision (aw_revision) is kept separate from the evaluator revision (AW_ACTION_REF). The 64-path limit, the 262144-byte per-file limit, the 4 MiB packet limit and the re-checks after the model all hold, and missing or invalid evidence blocks or stops the run. The hosted control job passed at this head. The remaining gap is local data. claude_review.trusted_skill() reads plugins/faberline/skills/issue-conformance/SKILL.md, and both the candidate controller and the evaluator reach it: native_merge and policy_adoption call review.verify_* → collect → trusted_skill, and invoke_json uses it as the system prompt. That file is not supplied at either revision. The closure check also cannot catch it: it only recognises sibling(), ci_module() and with_name() calls, not Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "...". The roster test therefore passes even though local data is missing.

requirement_results.evidence: supporting_sources uses MAX_SUPPORTING_PATHS=64 and still requires distinct paths that pass valid_path. Each path must exist at base or head, or the run stops with target_supporting_source_missing. source_entry and review.blob enforce the 262144-byte limit and the blob identity, and the size is checked again after reading (target_supporting_truncated). The packet is checked against 4 MiB in preflight and again by invoke_schema with max_packet=4 MiB, which blocks if exceeded. Nothing is dropped or truncated silently.

framework_sources reads FRAMEWORK_SOURCES from faberline/aw with review.blob, which checks the GitHub sha against the computed Git blob. Each row records role, repo, ref, path, blob and content, and the candidate (aw_revision) and evaluator (AW_ACTION_REF) roles are separate. Nothing is executed. However, local data the controllers actually read is missing. claude_review.trusted_skill reads skills/issue-conformance/SKILL.md, and both native_merge (through verify_result_receipt → collect) and the evaluator (through policy_adoption → native/review) reach it. It is not supplied at either revision.

preflight now includes shared_framework_sources. produce re-runs preflight before the final review (fresh==initial) and after the model (final==initial), so any change in source, PR, issue, CI, provider or framework data blocks or stops the run. A failure to read a framework file or verify its identity in preflight raises an error and produces no receipt.

The planning-question handling, the candidate_evidence CI checks, base_rules with zero bypass actors, the separate-grant wording in SYSTEM and the held-product-acceptance wording are unchanged. The only prompt change mentions the 64-path limit and the separately supplied framework source. No candidate code runs with credentials.

New tests cover rosters of 41 and 64 paths (no truncation), 65 paths and '../unsafe' (both rejected), absent paths (existing test), pinned framework blob identity including a non-hex ref and a corrupted sha (source_identity), the 4 MiB packet limit in preflight, and a closure test for sibling, ci_module and with_name. The hosted job 'complete isolated native merge controls' passed at this head.

All transitive sibling modules are present at both revisions, and the closure test detects omitted sibling, ci_module and with_name targets. The issue-conformance/SKILL.md local data, read through parents[2] path joining, is neither included nor detected. test_framework_roster_covers_current_entrypoint_dependency_closure passes only because the check does not detect this pattern.

findings.title: Local data read by the controller (issue-conformance/SKILL.md) is not supplied, and the closure check cannot detect it
findings.detail: claude_review.trusted_skill() reads Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]/'issue-conformance/SKILL.md' and verifies it against SKILL_SHA256. collect() calls it on every review verification. The candidate controller reaches it (native_merge enqueue/return_todo → verify_result_receipt → collect), and so does the evaluator through the same claude_review module. invoke_json also uses it as the system prompt. FRAMEWORK_SOURCES (COMMON_FRAMEWORK_FILES and EVALUATOR_FRAMEWORK_FILES) only lists files in FRAMEWORK_ROOT (issue-ci/scripts/), so this local data is missing at both pinned revisions. framework_dependency_closure (around line 62) only recognises sibling(), ci_module() and with_name() calls with constant arguments. It cannot detect path joins such as parents[N] / '...' or ROOT / '...', so the omission passes the check and the roster test. The human scope extension explicitly requires all transitive local data at both revisions, plus closure tests that detect omissions.
findings.required_fix: Allow framework entries outside scripts/ and add plugins/faberline/skills/issue-conformance/SKILL.md to the files read at both the candidate and evaluator revisions, with the same blob binding. Extend framework_dependency_closure to detect other local file reads, such as Path(__file__).parents[...] / '<const>' and module-root / '<const>' joins, or to refuse any unrecognised local file reference. Add a test where omitting SKILL.md, or another file referenced that way, raises target_framework_dependency_missing.
